title: Others teach images of God and Christ are to be adored with latria—yet call it relative or per accidens, so Councils still ‘agree’
source_text: XXXI. Contra vero inter eos qui in Schola Romana eminent reperiuntur multi, qui non docent simpliciter imagines esse adorandas, sed pertendunt imagines Dei Christique esse adorandas latria, quo nomine Schola Romana designare solet summum illum cultum qui Deo proprius est. Cum tamen Ecclesiae Romanae Concilia a latria sedulo distinguant adorationem quam volunt imaginibus Christi & Sanctorum deferri, ut pluribus ante ostendimus. Sed nec illi videri volunt a Conciliis illis dissentire, & sententiam suam cum Synodorum suarum definitionibus conciliari facile posse putant. Nempe dicunt imagines Dei Christique latria quidem esse colendas, non tamen propter se, sed propter prototypa, adeoque latriam illam, non absolutam, sed relativam esse; aut saltem cultum latriae illis deferri, non per se, sed per accidens, quatenus considerantur cum prototypo junctae, & unum quid cum illo constituentes. Jam vero Concilia quae nullis Imaginibus latriam deferri volunt, intelligenda esse de latria absoluta, non vero de relativa; aut de latria per se, non de latria per accidens.
pass_a_gloss: But on the contrary, among those who are eminent in the Roman School many are found who do not teach simply that images are to be adored, but maintain that the images of God and of Christ are to be adored with latria, by which name the Roman School is accustomed to designate that supreme cult which is proper to God. Yet the Councils of the Roman Church carefully distinguish from latria the adoration which they will to have paid to the images of Christ and of the Saints, as we showed above at length. But neither do those men wish to appear to dissent from those Councils, and they think their opinion can easily be reconciled with their Synods’ definitions. Namely they say that the images of God and of Christ are indeed to be cultivated with latria, yet not on their own account but on account of the prototypes, and so that latria is not absolute but relative; or at least that the cult of latria is paid to them not per se but per accidens, insofar as they are considered joined with the prototype and constituting one thing with it. And now the Councils which will have latria paid to no Images are to be understood of absolute latria, not of relative; or of latria per se, not of latria per accidens.
pass_b_english: Some leading Schoolmen even assign latria to images of God and Christ.
They salvage Council language by calling that latria relative or per accidens—joined to the prototype—not absolute latria per se.

choices.why: School device to give images latria without ‘dissenting’ from Councils.
rejected: flat latria to paint as God
